title: Normalized scalar exchange data for derived coinduction
statement:
Let $R,A,T,B$ be commutative rings, with ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and ring maps $f:R\to A$, $g:R\to T$, $a:A\to B$, $b:T\to B$. A scalar pair for a ring map $h:S\to S'$ is a functor $F_h:D(S)\to D(S')$ with a universal left-derived counit $Q_SF_h\to (S'\otimes_S-)Q_{S'}$, invertible on K-flat complexes, presenting derived scalar extension [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Write $U_f,U_b$ for derived restriction and $C_f,C_b$ for derived coinduction [def-trf-derived-coinduction], with their evaluation counits $\epsilon_f,\epsilon_b$. Given scalar pairs $d_g,d_a$ and a natural isomorphism $\theta:d_a.F\,U_b\simeq U_f\,d_g.F$ (composition written left to right), define the following exchange data and predicates.

The tensor normalization of $\theta$ is the equation on every K-flat $A$-complex $E$ identifying $\theta^{-1}$, via the two scalar-pair counits and the restriction/localization comparisons, with the localization of each ordinary balancing isomorphism $e:T\otimes_R U_fE\simeq U_b(B\otimes_A E)$ having $e(t\otimes x)=b(t)\otimes x$.

For $M\in D(R)$ define $\gamma_M:d_a.F(C_fM)\to C_b(d_g.FM)$ to be the adjoint of $\theta_{C_fM}$ followed by $d_g.F(\epsilon_{f,M})$, using the restriction/coinduction adjunction. Thus the actual $B$-action is retained.

For complexes $E,Q$ over $R$, an augmentation $s:E\to U_fA[0]$, and an isomorphism $e:Q_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(E,Q)\simeq U_fC_f(Q_RQ)$, define its Hom model predicate using the module-valued total Hom complex [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] as follows: for every K-injective complex $I$ and every map $l:Q\to I$, there exist the postcomposition chain map $j(z)=l\circ z$, the augmentation-precomposition chain map $p(z)=z\circ s$, and the canonical complex coinduction/Hom isomorphism $k$. Require the localized equation
$$Q_R(j)=e\circ U_fC_f(Q_Rl)\circ U_f(\mathrm{model}_f(I))\circ\mathrm{restriction\ comparison}\circ Q_R(k)\circ Q_R(p),$$
where this displayed composition is written in order of application. The coordinates of $k$ send a coinduced element $z$ to $x\mapsto z(x)$ under the ordinary coinduction/linear-Hom equivalence.

For a chain map
$$\chi:T\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(E,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}_T^\bullet(T\otimes_RE,T\otimes_RQ),$$
define the Hom scalar formula predicate to require, in every homogeneous coordinate $r+n=t$, every $z\in\operatorname{Hom}_R^n(E,Q)$, $x\in E^r$, and $v,w\in T$,
$$(\chi(v\otimes z))_{r,t}(w\otimes x)=vw\otimes z_{r,t}(x).$$

For composable ring maps $h:S\to S'$, $h':S'\to S''$ and scalar pairs $d,e,c$ for $h,h',h'h$, define scalar-composition normalization of $\alpha:d.F\,e.F\simeq c.F$ to mean that on each K-flat $S$-complex its hom followed by $c$'s counit equals the successive counits followed by the localization of the inverse ordinary tensor associator.

Finally define the tower predicate for $(f,g,a,b,d_g,d_a,\theta)$: for every further pushout square $T\xrightarrow{t}V$, $B\xrightarrow{j}C$, $V\xrightarrow{c}C$ with maps from $T$ given by $b,t$, every scalar pair for $t,j,tg,ja$, and every derived Tor-independent identification $F_{tg}(U_fA[0])\simeq U_cC[0]$, there exist normalized scalar associators $\alpha_R:F_gF_t\simeq F_{tg}$, $\alpha_A:F_aF_j\simeq F_{ja}$ and normalized tensor comparisons $\theta',\theta''$ for the direct and second squares such that for every unbounded $M\in D(R)$,
$$\alpha_A^{-1}(C_fM)\,;\,F_j(\gamma_M)\,;\,\gamma''_{F_gM}\,;\,C_c(\alpha_R(M))=\gamma'_M.$$
These are definitions of data, maps and predicates; they assert neither existence of the tensor comparisons nor invertibility of the counit mates.
